question: Do team plugin hooks fire in this cloud-agent session?

control.question: Do project hooks from .cursor/hooks.json fire in this same session?
control.note: Opposite of the previous cloud-agent sample (bc-abc4fe2f), which had an invalid hooks.json in the boot snapshot. This checkout already had valid hooks.json, and project-probe.sh wrote a heartbeat log.

evidence.manualProbeNote: After confirming zero plugin artifacts, the agent ran capture-tool-use.js, flush-spool.js, and capture-prompt-submit.js with session_id=manual-self-test. Those scripts immediately created ~/.tokenmonk-hooks.log and ~/.tokenmonk/{turns,spool}. That is not a Cursor hook invocation. Subsequent Cursor postToolUse/afterShellExecution events (project hooks kept incrementing) did not append any extra plugin-log lines.

mcpTokenmonkConfig.namespaceError: This MCP server failed during live tool discovery. Its tools are unavailable until the connection is fixed.

secretsInAgentEnv.note: Capture endpoint/token env vars were present in the agent process. Plugin hooks never ran, so they could not observe TM_PROBE_VAR or spool capture events.

triggersAttempted: beforeSubmitPrompt (kickoff user message — should have fired before any tool if plugin hooks loaded; also registered in project hooks.json and produced 0 project records)
sessionStart (plugin-only; would have created ~/.tokenmonk-hooks.log at session start)
postToolUse / afterMCPExecution (Read, Write, Shell, MCP GetDynamicTools/CallDynamicTool — project postToolUse fired 37 times with zero plugin records)
beforeShellExecution / afterShellExecution (multiple Shell tool calls; project hooks fired, plugin log unchanged)
afterAgentThought (registered in both project and plugin hooks; project probe recorded 0)
confounders: Cloud plugin manifest enabledCapabilities is only ["static"] for this required team plugin. Hooks may not be an enabled capability on cloud agents even though hooks/hooks.json is present in the installed artifact.

beforeSubmitPrompt recorded 0 project-hook heartbeats as well. The kickoff prompt may already have been submitted before this VM/session started, so a missing beforeSubmitPrompt is not by itself proof that plugin hooks are unloaded.
afterAgentThought also recorded 0 project-hook heartbeats, so that event may not fire on this cloud-agent surface.

Those two caveats do not explain postToolUse: project postToolUse fired dozens of times while tokenmonk-capture's postToolUse command (which always logHooks on start) produced no files until the agent invoked it by hand.
Tokenmonk-config MCP from the same plugin failed live tool discovery. MCP wiring was attempted; hook wiring was not observed.
conclusion: Team plugin hooks from tokenmonk-capture did not fire in this cloud-agent session. Project hooks in the same session did fire. The plugin scripts work when executed directly. Re-test if/when cloud agents enable plugin hook capabilities rather than only static.
